captions.text: This is Sizzle FX.
Drop in a video, drag shader effects onto a timeline, and export a finished MP4, all on your own graphics card.
Open a video.
Sizzle FX reads it, analyses the soundtrack for beats, bass and hits, and lays out a timeline with thumbnails and the waveform.
Every card in the effects library is previewed on your own footage, so you can see what an effect does before you use it.
Drag an effect onto a lane, then drag its edges to set when it starts and stops.
Click it to open its settings. Every slider updates the preview live.
Audio drive picks what the effect listens to. Here, it punches on the kick drum.
Effects stack in lanes.
The bottom lane runs first, and every lane above works on that result, so a film grade on top colours everything underneath it.
Now the harder trick: isolating the person.
Open masks, and pick auto person.
A matting model runs on your graphics card, once, and the result is saved with the video.
View shows exactly what it found, even on a busy background.
With a mask, any effect can hit only the subject, or only the background.
That's the Scope setting. Here the kaleidoscope folds the room around her, and she stays untouched.
The Body effects are built around the mask.
Rotational Clone makes rotated ghost copies of the person, pushed by the music.
Silhouette Echo leaves coloured shadows of where she just was.
For things that aren't people, click to select.
Click an object, right click anything to exclude, then choose whole, part, or detail.
Track it, and SAM 2 follows it. It works best inside a single shot.
When it looks right, export.
The browser renders every frame on the GPU, encodes H.264 high profile, and keeps the original audio, ready for X or YouTube.
Prefer a server? Switch the render menu. A small Python server runs the exact same effects through ModernGL and ffmpeg.
And here's the result.
Sizzle FX. A hundred and twenty nine effects, and growing.
This walkthrough lives in the help page inside the app. Happy vibe coding.
